title: Rishtan ceramics
summary: Potters of Rishtan, in the Fergana valley, throw broad plates and bowls from local red clay and paint them with an alkaline ash glaze that fires to deep turquoise, cobalt and green. The big serving plate, called a lagan, can be a metre across.
howToPlay: Study the plate in the frame: a small foot, a sloping wall and a wide rim.
Drag across each row of spinning clay to set its width.
Press Glaze, choose a colour and fill the four bands from the centre outward.
Press Check when the plate and its glaze match.
rules: Eight rows of clay, each from one to twelve steps wide.
Seventy points for the shape and thirty for the glaze bands.
Three stars need a nearly exact plate with its colours in order.
heritageNote: Potters of the Fergana valley have made glazed ware at Rishtan for centuries, drawing flowers and leaves from nature in blue-green glaze made from the ash of desert plants. Workshops pass the craft from parent to child, and the glaze was revived in the 1970s.
